It's one of the "Paradise Worlds," terraformed to have a perfect climate, accessible only to the very wealthy. You wonder whether James is going to be able to fit in there.|143|0
units.english: Once again you walk back to your ship with James. Once you get there, as he's stowing his luggage, you pull up the information your computer has on <planet>. It's one of the "Paradise Worlds," terraformed to have a perfect climate, accessible only to the very wealthy. You wonder whether James is going to be able to fit in there.
units.italian: Ancora una volta torni alla nave con James. Una volta arrivati, mentre lui sistema i bagagli, richiami le informazioni che il computer ha su <planet>. È uno dei "Mondi Paradisiaci", terraformato per avere un clima perfetto, accessibile solo ai molto ricchi. Ti chiedi se James riuscirà a inserirsi là.

units.id: conversation:intro earth offer|	Once again you walk back to your ship with James. You've heard of <planet> before; one of the Paradise Worlds terraformed from a lifeless ice planet to the largest and most luxurious retirement home in the galaxy. As you look at his utilitarian outfit and modest luggage, something seems off about the idea of James living in such a place.|146|0
units.english: Once again you walk back to your ship with James. You've heard of <planet> before; one of the Paradise Worlds terraformed from a lifeless ice planet to the largest and most luxurious retirement home in the galaxy. As you look at his utilitarian outfit and modest luggage, something seems off about the idea of James living in such a place.
units.italian: Ancora una volta torni alla nave con James. Hai già sentito parlare di <planet>: uno dei Mondi Paradisiaci, terraformato da un pianeta di ghiaccio senza vita nella casa di riposo più grande e lussuosa della galassia. Guardando il suo abbigliamento utilitario e i bagagli modesti, qualcosa non torna nell'idea di James che vive in un posto simile.

units.id: conversation:freighter 1 end|You drop off the shipment of <commodity> on <planet>, and collect your payment of <payment>. "Hauling freight," says James. "Not the most glamorous job, or the most interesting, but you're always guaranteed steady income. And once you know the galaxy a bit better, instead of taking missions you can find your own trade routes to follow. The only trouble is, build up a fleet with lots of cargo space and not enough defenses and the pirates begin to take notice."|152|0
units.english: You drop off the shipment of <commodity> on <planet>, and collect your payment of <payment>. "Hauling freight," says James. "Not the most glamorous job, or the most interesting, but you're always guaranteed steady income. And once you know the galaxy a bit better, instead of taking missions you can find your own trade routes to follow. The only trouble is, build up a fleet with lots of cargo space and not enough defenses and the pirates begin to take notice."
units.italian: Scarichi il carico di <commodity> su <planet> e incassi il pagamento di <payment>. "Trasporto merci," dice James. "Non è il lavoro più affascinante, né il più interessante, ma hai sempre un reddito costante garantito. E quando conoscerai un po' meglio la galassia, invece di prendere missioni potrai trovarti da solo le rotte commerciali da seguire. L'unico problema è che, se metti insieme una flotta con molto spazio di carico e difese insufficienti, i pirati cominciano a notarti."

units.id: conversation:freighter 1 end|	"Did you have a lot of trouble with pirates when you were a captain?"|154|0
units.english: "Did you have a lot of trouble with pirates when you were a captain?"
units.italian: "Hai avuto molti problemi con i pirati quando eri capitano?"

units.id: conversation:freighter 1 end|	"But what if I want to earn money more quickly than I can by trading?"|155|0
units.english: "But what if I want to earn money more quickly than I can by trading?"
units.italian: "Ma se volessi guadagnare più in fretta di quanto si guadagni commerciando?"

units.id: conversation:freighter 1 end|	"Some. That's why you can't just go traipsing around the galaxy in a fleet of unarmed star barges; every pirate within a week's travel will hear you're coming through and come after you. In the long term, having a few heavy freighters with good defenses is more cost-effective than losing a star barge or two to the pirates on every journey."|157|0
units.english: "Some. That's why you can't just go traipsing around the galaxy in a fleet of unarmed star barges; every pirate within a week's travel will hear you're coming through and come after you. In the long term, having a few heavy freighters with good defenses is more cost-effective than losing a star barge or two to the pirates on every journey."
units.italian: "Un po'. Ed è per questo che non puoi andartene in giro per la galassia con una flotta di chiatte stellari disarmate; ogni pirata a una settimana di viaggio sentirà che stai arrivando e ti verrà dietro. Sul lungo periodo, avere qualche mercantile pesante con buone difese costa meno che perdere una o due chiatte stellari ai pirati a ogni viaggio."

units.id: conversation:freighter 1 end|	"There's no quick road to riches, kid. The more something pays, the riskier it is. If you need to make lots of money in a hurry, bounty hunting is the way to go, but nine out of ten pilots who give bounty hunting a try end up dead. And no one's going to give you those sorts of missions until you've proved yourself in combat, anyway."|160|0
units.english: "There's no quick road to riches, kid. The more something pays, the riskier it is. If you need to make lots of money in a hurry, bounty hunting is the way to go, but nine out of ten pilots who give bounty hunting a try end up dead. And no one's going to give you those sorts of missions until you've proved yourself in combat, anyway."
units.italian: "Non c'è una strada rapida per arricchirsi, ragazzo. Più qualcosa paga, più è rischioso. Se devi fare molti soldi in fretta, la caccia alle taglie è la via, ma nove piloti su dieci che ci provano finiscono morti. E comunque nessuno ti darà quel tipo di missioni finché non ti sarai dimostrato in combattimento."

units.id: conversation:freighter 1 end|	He picks up his suitcase. "If you want to run another mission with me, look for me in the spaceport. I'll see if I can find you something with a higher profit margin this time."|162|0
units.english: He picks up his suitcase. "If you want to run another mission with me, look for me in the spaceport. I'll see if I can find you something with a higher profit margin this time."
units.italian: Raccoglie la valigia. "Se vuoi fare un'altra missione con me, cercami allo spazioporto. Vedrò di trovarti qualcosa con un margine di profitto più alto, questa volta."

units.id: conversation:freighter 1 end|	(As before, click the "Spaceport" button to continue this mission.)|164|0
units.english: (As before, click the "Spaceport" button to continue this mission.)
units.italian: (Come prima, per continuare questa missione premi il pulsante "Spazioporto".)

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|By now, your entire ship smells like brine and raw fish, but as best you can tell the fish is still fresh enough to eat. The dock workers on <planet> offload it without comment, and give you your payment of <payment>.|169|0
units.english: By now, your entire ship smells like brine and raw fish, but as best you can tell the fish is still fresh enough to eat. The dock workers on <planet> offload it without comment, and give you your payment of <payment>.
units.italian: Ormai tutta la nave puzza di salamoia e pesce crudo, ma per quanto puoi capire il pesce è ancora abbastanza fresco da mangiare. Gli scaricatori di <planet> lo sbarcano senza commenti e ti consegnano il pagamento di <payment>.

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|Your cargo has loomed silently in your hold for the last few days, but as far as you can tell, the samples are still safely contained. The dock workers on <planet> offload it without comment, and give you your payment of <payment>.|174|0
units.english: Your cargo has loomed silently in your hold for the last few days, but as far as you can tell, the samples are still safely contained. The dock workers on <planet> offload it without comment, and give you your payment of <payment>.
units.italian: Il tuo carico è rimasto silenzioso nella stiva per gli ultimi giorni, ma per quanto puoi capire i campioni sono ancora al sicuro. Gli scaricatori di <planet> lo sbarcano senza commenti e ti consegnano il pagamento di <payment>.

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|Your cargo has loomed silently in your hold for the last few days, but the radiation alarms in your ship's hold haven't let out a squeak. The dock workers on <planet> offload it quickly onto several waiting trains, and give you your payment of <payment>.|177|0
units.english: Your cargo has loomed silently in your hold for the last few days, but the radiation alarms in your ship's hold haven't let out a squeak. The dock workers on <planet> offload it quickly onto several waiting trains, and give you your payment of <payment>.
units.italian: Il tuo carico è rimasto silenzioso nella stiva per gli ultimi giorni, ma gli allarmi delle radiazioni non hanno fatto un fiato. Gli scaricatori di <planet> lo trasferiscono in fretta su diversi treni in attesa e ti consegnano il pagamento di <payment>.

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|	"If you can line them up right," says James, "rush deliveries can be your best source of income as a freighter captain. And keep your eye out for missions with large amounts of cargo, too, because your barge's hold is definitely big enough to handle them. And if you've got any cargo space to spare and you know what the prices are going to be at your destination, be sure to stock up on something you can sell for a profit."|181|0
units.english: "If you can line them up right," says James, "rush deliveries can be your best source of income as a freighter captain. And keep your eye out for missions with large amounts of cargo, too, because your barge's hold is definitely big enough to handle them. And if you've got any cargo space to spare and you know what the prices are going to be at your destination, be sure to stock up on something you can sell for a profit."
units.italian: "Se riesci a incastrarle bene," dice James, "le consegne urgenti possono essere la tua migliore fonte di reddito come capitano mercantile. E tieni d'occhio anche le missioni con grandi quantità di carico, perché la stiva della tua chiatta è decisamente abbastanza grande. E se ti avanza spazio e sai quali saranno i prezzi a destinazione, fai scorta di qualcosa che puoi rivendere con profitto."

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|	"What would you recommend if I want to do more than just carry cargo?"|183|0
units.english: "What would you recommend if I want to do more than just carry cargo?"
units.italian: "Che cosa mi consiglieresti se volessi fare più che trasportare carico?"

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|	"Did you do that for your whole career?"|184|0
units.english: "Did you do that for your whole career?"
units.italian: "L'hai fatto per tutta la carriera?"

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|	He pauses for a moment to think, then says, "Unless you want to do something really risky like hunting pirates, your best bet is to work with the Navy, or the Syndicate, or one of the local militias. Any of those would be a decent choice, although they've each got their own problems. If any of them offer you a mission, go ahead and take it; that's a good way to build connections and get to know the lay of the land."|186|0
units.english: He pauses for a moment to think, then says, "Unless you want to do something really risky like hunting pirates, your best bet is to work with the Navy, or the Syndicate, or one of the local militias. Any of those would be a decent choice, although they've each got their own problems. If any of them offer you a mission, go ahead and take it; that's a good way to build connections and get to know the lay of the land."
units.italian: Si ferma un momento a pensare, poi dice: "A meno che tu non voglia fare qualcosa di davvero rischioso come cacciare pirati, la tua opzione migliore è lavorare con la Marina, o con il Sindacato, o con una delle milizie locali. Ognuna sarebbe una scelta decente, anche se ognuna ha i suoi problemi. Se una di loro ti offre una missione, prendila: è un buon modo per costruire contatti e capire come gira il posto."

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|	"Well," he says, "Back when I was a bit older than you, I piloted a Firebird for a while, escorting merchant convoys up and down the Rim. I used to hope we'd get attacked; I'd disable the pirate ships and rob them blind. Turnabout is fair play, after all.|189|0
units.english: "Well," he says, "Back when I was a bit older than you, I piloted a Firebird for a while, escorting merchant convoys up and down the Rim. I used to hope we'd get attacked; I'd disable the pirate ships and rob them blind. Turnabout is fair play, after all.
units.italian: "Beh," dice, "quando avevo qualche anno più di te, ho pilotato un Firebird per un po', scortando convogli mercantili su e giù per il Rim. Speravo sempre che ci attaccassero; disattivavo le navi pirata e le depredavo. La ruota gira, dopo tutto.

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|	"Then one day I got a bit too greedy and thought I'd try to capture a pirate ship or two, to add more firepower to my fleet. We boarded their ship, and I sent my crew through the airlock to kill off the pirates. And it turns out the pirates had grenades. Four of my men were dead before I even realized what was happening. We had to retreat, and then limp back to port without even enough crew left uninjured to pilot the ship right. After that I decided to stick to less risky jobs."|190|0
units.english: "Then one day I got a bit too greedy and thought I'd try to capture a pirate ship or two, to add more firepower to my fleet. We boarded their ship, and I sent my crew through the airlock to kill off the pirates. And it turns out the pirates had grenades. Four of my men were dead before I even realized what was happening. We had to retreat, and then limp back to port without even enough crew left uninjured to pilot the ship right. After that I decided to stick to less risky jobs."
units.italian: "Poi un giorno sono stato un po' troppo avido e ho pensato di catturare una o due navi pirata, per aggiungere potenza di fuoco alla flotta. Siamo saliti a bordo della loro nave e ho mandato il mio equipaggio attraverso la camera stagna a eliminare i pirati. E si dà il caso che i pirati avessero le granate. Quattro dei miei erano morti prima che capissi che cosa stava succedendo. Abbiamo dovuto ritirarci e poi tornare zoppicando in porto senza nemmeno abbastanza equipaggio illeso per pilotare la nave come si deve. Dopo quella volta ho deciso di dedicarmi a lavori meno rischiosi."

units.id: conversation:freighter 2 end|	He glances toward the spaceport and says, "Anyway, if you want to make one more trip with me, you know where to find me."|192|0
units.english: He glances toward the spaceport and says, "Anyway, if you want to make one more trip with me, you know where to find me."
units.italian: Dà un'occhiata verso lo spazioporto e dice: "Comunque, se vuoi fare un altro viaggio con me, sai dove trovarmi."

units.id: conversation:intro ingot|You find James talking with a group of miners, who seem to be old acquaintances of his. As you approach, he says, "Well guys, here comes my ride. I should probably say goodbye." They head back off to do their work. "Every time I land here," says James, "I'm amazed that this station hasn't been wiped out yet by a meteorite. Can you imagine spending your life here?"|197|0
units.english: You find James talking with a group of miners, who seem to be old acquaintances of his. As you approach, he says, "Well guys, here comes my ride. I should probably say goodbye." They head back off to do their work. "Every time I land here," says James, "I'm amazed that this station hasn't been wiped out yet by a meteorite. Can you imagine spending your life here?"
units.italian: Trovi James che parla con un gruppo di minatori, che sembrano vecchie conoscenze. Mentre ti avvicini dice: "Beh ragazzi, ecco il mio passaggio. Credo che mi convenga salutare." Loro tornano al lavoro. "Ogni volta che atterro qui," dice James, "mi stupisco che questa stazione non sia ancora stata spazzata via da un meteorite. Riusciresti a immaginare di passare la vita qui?"

units.id: conversation:intro ingot|	"It does seem awfully isolated. But some people might enjoy the solitude."|199|0
units.english: "It does seem awfully isolated. But some people might enjoy the solitude."
units.italian: "Sembra terribilmente isolato. Ma ad alcuni potrebbe piacere la solitudine."

units.id: conversation:intro ingot|	"Well, if you need the money, at least it's a steady job."|200|0
units.english: "Well, if you need the money, at least it's a steady job."
units.italian: "Beh, se hai bisogno di soldi, almeno è un lavoro stabile."

units.id: conversation:intro ingot|	"I suppose," he says. "Anyway, I think it's time for the last leg of my journey. Do you think you can give me a lift to <planet>? I'll pay you quite well for your services, of course."|201|0
units.english: "I suppose," he says. "Anyway, I think it's time for the last leg of my journey. Do you think you can give me a lift to <planet>? I'll pay you quite well for your services, of course."
units.italian: "Suppongo di sì," dice. "Comunque, credo che sia tempo per l'ultima tappa del mio viaggio. Pensi di potermi portare su <planet>? Ti pagherò molto bene per i tuoi servizi, naturalmente."

units.id: conversation:intro ingot|	"I can take you there."|203|0
units.english: "I can take you there."
units.italian: "Posso portarti là."

units.id: conversation:intro ingot|	"Sorry, I was thinking of heading in a different direction from here."|204|0
units.english: "Sorry, I was thinking of heading in a different direction from here."
units.italian: "Spiacente, pensavo di andare in una direzione diversa da qui."

units.id: conversation:intro ingot|	Once again you walk back to your ship with James. Once you get there, as he's stowing his luggage, you pull up the information your computer has on <planet>. It's one of the "Paradise Worlds," terraformed to have a perfect climate, accessible only to the very wealthy. You wonder whether James is going to be able to fit in there.|206|0
units.english: Once again you walk back to your ship with James. Once you get there, as he's stowing his luggage, you pull up the information your computer has on <planet>. It's one of the "Paradise Worlds," terraformed to have a perfect climate, accessible only to the very wealthy. You wonder whether James is going to be able to fit in there.
units.italian: Ancora una volta torni alla nave con James. Una volta arrivati, mentre lui sistema i bagagli, richiami le informazioni che il computer ha su <planet>. È uno dei "Mondi Paradisiaci", terraformato per avere un clima perfetto, accessibile solo ai molto ricchi. Ti chiedi se James riuscirà a inserirsi là.

units.id: conversation:interceptor escort end|The captain of the <npc> hands you <payment> and thanks you for your escort services. From the expression on <their> face, you'd guess that <they're> feeling lucky to still be alive after entrusting the safety of <their> fleet to a rookie pilot like yourself.|212|0
units.english: The captain of the <npc> hands you <payment> and thanks you for your escort services. From the expression on <their> face, you'd guess that <they're> feeling lucky to still be alive after entrusting the safety of <their> fleet to a rookie pilot like yourself.
units.italian: Il capitano della <npc> ti consegna <payment> e ti ringrazia per i servizi di scorta. Dall'espressione sul volto, diresti che si sente fortunato a essere ancora vivo dopo aver affidato la sicurezza della sua flotta a un pilota alle prime armi come te.

units.id: conversation:interceptor escort end|	After <they are> gone, James turns to you and says, "Not too bad for your first escort mission. I recognize that look on your face - it's the same one I had after my first job like this back when I was a beginner. If I recall, my first priority after touching down was replacing some of the ship's guns with missile launchers so I'd actually have a chance against pirates. It's a scandal how they sell interceptors with nothing but short-ranged energy weapons these days; trying to use them in combat on such a small ship is practically suicide. Keep your distance with some missiles and you can almost never go wrong.|213|0
units.english: After <they are> gone, James turns to you and says, "Not too bad for your first escort mission. I recognize that look on your face - it's the same one I had after my first job like this back when I was a beginner. If I recall, my first priority after touching down was replacing some of the ship's guns with missile launchers so I'd actually have a chance against pirates. It's a scandal how they sell interceptors with nothing but short-ranged energy weapons these days; trying to use them in combat on such a small ship is practically suicide. Keep your distance with some missiles and you can almost never go wrong.
units.italian: Dopo che la nave si è allontanata, James si volta verso di te e dice: "Non male per la tua prima missione di scorta. Riconosco quell'espressione sul tuo viso: è la stessa che avevo io dopo il mio primo lavoro del genere, quando ero un principiante. Se ricordo bene, la mia prima priorità dopo l'atterraggio è stata sostituire alcuni cannoni della nave con lanciamissili, per avere davvero qualche possibilità contro i pirati. È uno scandalo come vendano gli intercettori con nient'altro che armi energetiche a corto raggio, oggigiorno; provare a usarli in combattimento su una nave così piccola è praticamente un suicidio. Tieni le distanze con qualche missile e quasi non puoi sbagliare.

units.id: conversation:interceptor escort end|	"Anyway, I'll stop rambling. If you've still got a hankering for some dangerous missions, come and find me in the spaceport before you leave." He picks up his suitcase and heads outside.|215|0
units.english: "Anyway, I'll stop rambling. If you've still got a hankering for some dangerous missions, come and find me in the spaceport before you leave." He picks up his suitcase and heads outside.
units.italian: "Comunque, smetto di blaterare. Se ti è ancora venuta voglia di missioni pericolose, vieni a cercarmi allo spazioporto prima di partire." Prende la valigia ed esce.

units.id: conversation:interceptor escort end|	"Anyway, I'll stop rambling." James pauses for a moment, then says, "I've got an idea for something you might want to try. Meet me in the spaceport bar in a little while."|218|0
units.english: "Anyway, I'll stop rambling." James pauses for a moment, then says, "I've got an idea for something you might want to try. Meet me in the spaceport bar in a little while."
units.italian: "Comunque, smetto di blaterare." James fa una pausa, poi dice: "Ho un'idea su qualcosa che potresti voler provare. Raggiungimi al bar dello spazioporto fra un po'."

units.id: conversation:interceptor escort end|	(As before, click the "Spaceport" button to continue this mission. The next mission will involve carrying cargo, so it will only show up if you have 10 tons of space free.)|227|0
units.english: (As before, click the "Spaceport" button to continue this mission. The next mission will involve carrying cargo, so it will only show up if you have 10 tons of space free.)
units.italian: (Come prima, per continuare premi "Spazioporto". La prossima missione comporterà il trasporto di carico, quindi comparirà solo se hai 10 tonnellate di spazio libero.)

units.id: conversation:interceptor escort end|	(The next mission will involve carrying a passenger, so it will only show up if you have all your bunks free.)|232|0
units.english: (The next mission will involve carrying a passenger, so it will only show up if you have all your bunks free.)
units.italian: (La prossima missione comporterà il trasporto di un passeggero, quindi comparirà solo se hai tutti i posti letto liberi.)

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|You find James in the spaceport bar, talking with a woman wearing a business suit. The expression on James' face is growing increasingly concerned as she speaks. Seeing you come in, he waves to you and you join them at the table.|245|0
units.english: You find James in the spaceport bar, talking with a woman wearing a business suit. The expression on James' face is growing increasingly concerned as she speaks. Seeing you come in, he waves to you and you join them at the table.
units.italian: Trovi James nel bar dello spazioporto, che parla con una donna in tailleur. L'espressione di James si fa sempre più preoccupata mentre lei parla. Vedendoti entrare, ti fa un cenno e ti unisci a loro al tavolo.

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Hello <first>," says James. "This is Marissa, a senior manager at the mines." You shake hands with her.|246|0
units.english: "Hello <first>," says James. "This is Marissa, a senior manager at the mines." You shake hands with her.
units.italian: "Ciao <first>," dice James. "Lei è Marissa, dirigente delle miniere." Le stringi la mano.

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Here's the deal," says Marissa. "Most of the gemstones we mine here are industrial grade, not pretty enough to be worth using as anything but sandpaper grit or drill bits. But every once in a while we happen on some higher quality gems. No one in this sector has the money to spend on jewelry, so we ship them north to the Paradise Worlds.|247|0
units.english: "Here's the deal," says Marissa. "Most of the gemstones we mine here are industrial grade, not pretty enough to be worth using as anything but sandpaper grit or drill bits. But every once in a while we happen on some higher quality gems. No one in this sector has the money to spend on jewelry, so we ship them north to the Paradise Worlds.
units.italian: "Ecco la situazione," dice Marissa. "La maggior parte delle gemme che estraiamo qui è di grado industriale, non abbastanza bella da valere qualcosa oltre che come abrasivo o punta da trapano. Ma ogni tanto ci capita qualche gemma di qualità superiore. In questo settore nessuno ha i soldi per comprare gioielli, quindi le spediamo a nord, verso i Mondi Paradisiaci.

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"But in the past few months, every shipment we've sent has been attacked by a pirate ship, the Hammer of Thor. We don't have the money to pay a bounty hunter to take out the Hammer, so instead we're going to pay you to outrun it. Is the <ship> a fast ship?"|248|0
units.english: "But in the past few months, every shipment we've sent has been attacked by a pirate ship, the Hammer of Thor. We don't have the money to pay a bounty hunter to take out the Hammer, so instead we're going to pay you to outrun it. Is the <ship> a fast ship?"
units.italian: "Ma negli ultimi mesi ogni spedizione che abbiamo mandato è stata attaccata da una nave pirata, il Martello di Thor. Non abbiamo i soldi per pagare un cacciatore di taglie che elimini il Martello, quindi ti pagheremo per seminarlo. La <ship> è una nave veloce?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"As fast as they come. Nothing bigger than a fighter could chase it down."|250|0
units.english: "As fast as they come. Nothing bigger than a fighter could chase it down."
units.italian: "Veloce come poche. Niente di più grande di un caccia potrebbe inseguirla."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Not fast enough. I don't think I can risk taking on this mission."|251|0
units.english: "Not fast enough. I don't think I can risk taking on this mission."
units.italian: "Non abbastanza veloce. Non credo di poter rischiare questa missione."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Great," she says. "My people will load up your ship immediately. Good luck, Captain."|253|0
units.english: "Great," she says. "My people will load up your ship immediately. Good luck, Captain."
units.italian: "Ottimo," dice lei. "La mia gente caricherà subito la tua nave. Buona fortuna, Capitano."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|You end up finding James in a bar talking to a woman in a military uniform. "Nice to see you, <first>," he says. "I've been talking to Lieutenant Engberg over here, and I think we have a job on our hands."|257|0
units.english: You end up finding James in a bar talking to a woman in a military uniform. "Nice to see you, <first>," he says. "I've been talking to Lieutenant Engberg over here, and I think we have a job on our hands."
units.italian: Finisci per trovare James in un bar che parla con una donna in uniforme militare. "Bello vederti, <first>," dice. "Stavo parlando con il tenente Engberg, qui, e credo che abbiamo un lavoro per le mani."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"What is it?"|259|0
units.english: "What is it?"
units.italian: "Di che si tratta?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"You haven't drafted me into the Navy, have you?"|261|0
units.english: "You haven't drafted me into the Navy, have you?"
units.italian: "Non mi hai arruolato nella Marina, vero?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Actually, I want to go out on my own now."|262|0
units.english: "Actually, I want to go out on my own now."
units.italian: "In realtà, adesso voglio andare per conto mio."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	Engberg chuckles. "Firstly, I'm not part of the Navy, I'm with Deep Security. And secondly, not to disparage your abilities, but we only recruit experienced captains into our ranks."|264|0
units.english: Engberg chuckles. "Firstly, I'm not part of the Navy, I'm with Deep Security. And secondly, not to disparage your abilities, but we only recruit experienced captains into our ranks."
units.italian: Engberg ridacchia. "Primo, non faccio parte della Marina, sono della Sicurezza del Deep. Secondo, senza voler sminuire le tue capacità, noi arruoliamo solo capitani esperti."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	James says, "Deep Security mainly acts as the Deep equivalent of the Navy, protecting merchants from pirates. However, they also deal with the transport of confidential documents and equipment, for both the private and government sector."|266|0
units.english: James says, "Deep Security mainly acts as the Deep equivalent of the Navy, protecting merchants from pirates. However, they also deal with the transport of confidential documents and equipment, for both the private and government sector."
units.italian: James dice: "La Sicurezza del Deep è in pratica l'equivalente della Marina nel Deep: protegge i mercanti dai pirati. Però si occupa anche del trasporto di documenti e attrezzature riservate, sia per il settore privato sia per quello governativo."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	Engberg continues. "Recently, one of our logistics ships was attacked and damaged by a merchant warship named the Arm of Odin. We now believe that ship to be a pirate vessel in disguise, specifically targeting the cargo onboard. We're looking for a replacement ship capable of avoiding the threat while we track down the warlord. How fast would you say the <ship> is?"|267|0
units.english: Engberg continues. "Recently, one of our logistics ships was attacked and damaged by a merchant warship named the Arm of Odin. We now believe that ship to be a pirate vessel in disguise, specifically targeting the cargo onboard. We're looking for a replacement ship capable of avoiding the threat while we track down the warlord. How fast would you say the <ship> is?"
units.italian: Engberg continua. "Di recente una delle nostre navi logistiche è stata attaccata e danneggiata da una nave da guerra mercantile chiamata Braccio di Odino. Ora crediamo che quella nave sia un vascello pirata camuffato, che punta specificamente al carico. Cerchiamo una nave sostitutiva in grado di evitare la minaccia mentre diamo la caccia al signore della guerra. Quanto diresti che sia veloce la <ship>?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"It'll outspeed anything short of a fighter."|269|0
units.english: "It'll outspeed anything short of a fighter."
units.italian: "È più veloce di qualsiasi cosa che non sia un caccia."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Not fast enough. You'll have to find someone else for the job."|270|0
units.english: "Not fast enough. You'll have to find someone else for the job."
units.italian: "Non abbastanza veloce. Dovrai trovare qualcun altro per il lavoro."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Good," she says. "We'll have the cargo loaded onto your ship by sundown."|272|0
units.english: "Good," she says. "We'll have the cargo loaded onto your ship by sundown."
units.italian: "Bene," dice. "Faremo caricare il carico sulla tua nave entro il tramonto."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|For a planet so close to the Paradise Worlds, <origin> could not be any more different. Where the Paradise Worlds have meticulously preplanned cities, <origin> was designed by immediate needs. Where the Paradise Worlds cover themselves with nature and sculptures, <origin> bares itself to the galaxy, indulging in concrete pillars and steel trusses. Where the Paradise Worlds believe themselves to be untouchable utopias, <origin> is hardly afraid to show the scars of battle, its turrets and Navy garrisons in full display.|276|0
units.english: For a planet so close to the Paradise Worlds, <origin> could not be any more different. Where the Paradise Worlds have meticulously preplanned cities, <origin> was designed by immediate needs. Where the Paradise Worlds cover themselves with nature and sculptures, <origin> bares itself to the galaxy, indulging in concrete pillars and steel trusses. Where the Paradise Worlds believe themselves to be untouchable utopias, <origin> is hardly afraid to show the scars of battle, its turrets and Navy garrisons in full display.
units.italian: Per un pianeta così vicino ai Mondi Paradisiaci, <origin> non potrebbe essere più diverso. Dove i Mondi Paradisiaci hanno città meticolosamente preprogettate, <origin> è stato disegnato dalle necessità immediate. Dove i Mondi Paradisiaci si coprono di natura e sculture, <origin> si mostra nudo alla galassia, abbandonandosi a piloni di cemento e travi d'acciaio. Dove i Mondi Paradisiaci si credono utopie intoccabili, <origin> non teme affatto di mostrare le cicatrici della battaglia, con le sue torrette e le guarnigioni della Marina in bella vista.

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	You end up finding James in one of the cleaner bars, talking to a man in a Navy uniform. "Nice to see you, <first>," he says. "I've been talking to Lieutenant Armen over here, and I think we have a job on our hands."|277|0
units.english: You end up finding James in one of the cleaner bars, talking to a man in a Navy uniform. "Nice to see you, <first>," he says. "I've been talking to Lieutenant Armen over here, and I think we have a job on our hands."
units.italian: Finisci per trovare James in uno dei bar più puliti, che parla con un uomo in uniforme della Marina. "Bello vederti, <first>," dice. "Stavo parlando con il tenente Armen, qui, e credo che abbiamo un lavoro per le mani."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"What is it?"|279|0
units.english: "What is it?"
units.italian: "Di che si tratta?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"You haven't drafted me into the Navy, have you?"|281|0
units.english: "You haven't drafted me into the Navy, have you?"
units.italian: "Non mi hai arruolato nella Marina, vero?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Actually, I want to go out on my own now."|282|0
units.english: "Actually, I want to go out on my own now."
units.italian: "In realtà, adesso voglio andare per conto mio."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	Armen grins. "You would have a lot more to do if you were joining the Navy."|284|0
units.english: Armen grins. "You would have a lot more to do if you were joining the Navy."
units.italian: Armen sogghigna. "Se entrassi nella Marina avresti molto più da fare."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|label|285|0
units.english: job 2
units.italian: job 2

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	James says, "More than ever, the Republic Navy is struggling to hold off the threat of piracy. While they are able to keep the Paradise Worlds safe, on the edges of the known galaxy, pirates readily outnumber Navy forces. There are more ways to stop piracy than sheer force, however."|286|0
units.english: James says, "More than ever, the Republic Navy is struggling to hold off the threat of piracy. While they are able to keep the Paradise Worlds safe, on the edges of the known galaxy, pirates readily outnumber Navy forces. There are more ways to stop piracy than sheer force, however."
units.italian: James dice: "Ora più che mai la Marina della Repubblica fatica a contenere la minaccia della pirateria. Riescono a tenere al sicuro i Mondi Paradisiaci, ma ai margini della galassia conosciuta i pirati superano facilmente le forze della Marina. Ci sono però più modi per fermare la pirateria che la sola forza."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	Armen continues. "Which is where you come in. Recently, we've come into contact with someone claiming to have information on pirate activity in the North. If they're telling the truth, their knowledge could open the way for preemptive strikes against the pirates, freeing ships to be deployed elsewhere. However, the informant's existence has leaked, and a hired ship named the Eye of Loki is trying to cover up this loose end. We're looking for a ship able to outspeed the Eye and bring the informant safely to Pearl; we can handle transport from there. How fast would you say the <ship> is?"|287|0
units.english: Armen continues. "Which is where you come in. Recently, we've come into contact with someone claiming to have information on pirate activity in the North. If they're telling the truth, their knowledge could open the way for preemptive strikes against the pirates, freeing ships to be deployed elsewhere. However, the informant's existence has leaked, and a hired ship named the Eye of Loki is trying to cover up this loose end. We're looking for a ship able to outspeed the Eye and bring the informant safely to Pearl; we can handle transport from there. How fast would you say the <ship> is?"
units.italian: Armen continua. "Ed è qui che entri in gioco tu. Di recente siamo entrati in contatto con qualcuno che sostiene di avere informazioni sull'attività dei pirati nel Nord. Se dice la verità, le sue conoscenze potrebbero aprire la strada a colpi preventivi contro i pirati, liberando navi da schierare altrove. Però l'esistenza dell'informatore è trapelata, e una nave ingaggiata, l'Occhio di Loki, sta cercando di eliminare questo testimone scomodo. Cerchiamo una nave capace di seminare l'Occhio e portare l'informatore sano e salvo su Pearl; al trasporto da lì pensiamo noi. Quanto diresti che sia veloce la <ship>?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"It'll outspeed anything short of a fighter."|289|0
units.english: "It'll outspeed anything short of a fighter."
units.italian: "È più veloce di qualsiasi cosa che non sia un caccia."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Not fast enough. You'll have to find someone else for the job."|290|0
units.english: "Not fast enough. You'll have to find someone else for the job."
units.italian: "Non abbastanza veloce. Dovrai trovare qualcun altro per il lavoro."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Good," he says. "I'll have the informant on your ship by sundown."|292|0
units.english: "Good," he says. "I'll have the informant on your ship by sundown."
units.italian: "Bene," dice. "Farò salire l'informatore sulla tua nave entro il tramonto."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|You find James in the spaceport bar, talking with a man wearing a business suit. The expression on James' face is growing increasingly concerned as he speaks. Seeing you come in, he waves to you and you join them at the table.|296|0
units.english: You find James in the spaceport bar, talking with a man wearing a business suit. The expression on James' face is growing increasingly concerned as he speaks. Seeing you come in, he waves to you and you join them at the table.
units.italian: Trovi James nel bar dello spazioporto, che parla con un uomo in abito da ufficio. L'espressione di James si fa sempre più preoccupata mentre lui parla. Vedendoti entrare, ti fa un cenno e ti unisci a loro al tavolo.

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Hello <first>," says James. "This is Miguel, an independent mine owner on <origin>." Miguel smiles at you.|297|0
units.english: "Hello <first>," says James. "This is Miguel, an independent mine owner on <origin>." Miguel smiles at you.
units.italian: "Ciao <first>," dice James. "Lui è Miguel, proprietario indipendente di una miniera su <origin>." Miguel ti sorride.

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Here's the deal," says Miguel. "Most of the mining companies on <origin> have ties to the Syndicate, whether that be through direct ownership or indirect influence. Not us, though; my company's been resistant to any attempts of a takeover. One of their controlling techniques is preventing us from shipping our minerals to refineries within the Syndicate. However, there's nothing stopping us from shipping materials elsewhere in the galaxy, like magnetic elements for Lovelace's particle accelerators."|298|0
units.english: "Here's the deal," says Miguel. "Most of the mining companies on <origin> have ties to the Syndicate, whether that be through direct ownership or indirect influence. Not us, though; my company's been resistant to any attempts of a takeover. One of their controlling techniques is preventing us from shipping our minerals to refineries within the Syndicate. However, there's nothing stopping us from shipping materials elsewhere in the galaxy, like magnetic elements for Lovelace's particle accelerators."
units.italian: "Ecco la situazione," dice Miguel. "La maggior parte delle compagnie minerarie su <origin> ha legami con il Sindacato, per proprietà diretta o per influenza indiretta. Noi no; la mia compagnia ha resistito a ogni tentativo di acquisizione. Una delle loro tecniche di controllo è impedirci di spedire i minerali alle raffinerie del Sindacato. Però nessuno può impedirci di spedire materiali altrove nella galassia, per esempio elementi magnetici per gli acceleratori di particelle di Lovelace."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"But in the past few months, every shipment we've sent has been attacked by a pirate ship, the Spear of Heimdall. I doubt Syndicated Security would be keen on helping a rival company, so instead we're going to pay you to outrun it. Can you do that for us?"|299|0
units.english: "But in the past few months, every shipment we've sent has been attacked by a pirate ship, the Spear of Heimdall. I doubt Syndicated Security would be keen on helping a rival company, so instead we're going to pay you to outrun it. Can you do that for us?"
units.italian: "Ma negli ultimi mesi ogni spedizione che abbiamo mandato è stata attaccata da una nave pirata, la Lancia di Heimdall. Dubito che la Sicurezza del Sindacato abbia voglia di aiutare una compagnia rivale, quindi ti pagheremo per seminarla. Puoi farlo per noi?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"If you're willing to pay, I'm willing to fly."|301|0
units.english: "If you're willing to pay, I'm willing to fly."
units.italian: "Se sei disposto a pagare, sono disposto a volare."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"I got into the starship business to get away from people like you. Count me out."|302|0
units.english: "I got into the starship business to get away from people like you. Count me out."
units.italian: "Sono entrato nel settore delle navi stellari per allontanarmi da gente come te. Non contare su di me."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Great," he says. "My people will load up your ship immediately. Good luck, Captain."|304|0
units.english: "Great," he says. "My people will load up your ship immediately. Good luck, Captain."
units.italian: "Ottimo," dice lui. "La mia gente caricherà subito la tua nave. Buona fortuna, Capitano."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	After <person> leaves, James says to you, "Now, get one thing clear. This is not your David and Goliath moment. The <enemy>'s shields are <magnitude> times as strong as yours, and if it's able to bring its weapons to bear, we'll be dead in two seconds. So, the moment we're in the sky, we head straight for hyperspace. Don't even wait around to see if the <enemy> is coming or not. Got it?"|307|0
units.english: After <person> leaves, James says to you, "Now, get one thing clear. This is not your David and Goliath moment. The <enemy>'s shields are <magnitude> times as strong as yours, and if it's able to bring its weapons to bear, we'll be dead in two seconds. So, the moment we're in the sky, we head straight for hyperspace. Don't even wait around to see if the <enemy> is coming or not. Got it?"
units.italian: Dopo che <person> se n'è andato, James ti dice: "Ora, mettiamo in chiaro una cosa. Questo non è il tuo momento da Davide contro Golia. Gli scudi della <enemy> sono <magnitude> volte più forti dei tuoi, e se riesce a puntarti contro le armi siamo morti in due secondi. Quindi, appena siamo in cielo, andiamo dritti all'iperspazio. Non aspettare nemmeno di vedere se la <enemy> sta arrivando o no. Chiaro?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"Got it."|309|0
units.english: "Got it."
units.italian: "Chiaro."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"I really shouldn't try to fight?"|311|0
units.english: "I really shouldn't try to fight?"
units.italian: "Non dovrei davvero provare a combattere?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"It just isn't feasible," he says. "If a ship has turrets, your <model> can't get close enough to hit it with your guns without being damaged, and then it's just a matter of whose weapons and shields are stronger. If it has anti-missile turrets, you can't count on hanging back and bombarding it with missiles from long distances, or at least not with weapons that can fit in a <model>. So, don't risk it.|312|0
units.english: "It just isn't feasible," he says. "If a ship has turrets, your <model> can't get close enough to hit it with your guns without being damaged, and then it's just a matter of whose weapons and shields are stronger. If it has anti-missile turrets, you can't count on hanging back and bombarding it with missiles from long distances, or at least not with weapons that can fit in a <model>. So, don't risk it.
units.italian: "Semplicemente non è fattibile," dice. "Se una nave ha torrette, la tua <model> non può avvicinarsi abbastanza da colpirla con i cannoni senza essere danneggiata, e poi è solo questione di chi ha armi e scudi più forti. Se ha torrette antimissile, non puoi contare di restare indietro a bombardarla da lontano, o almeno non con armi che entrano in una <model>. Quindi non rischiare.

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade intro|	"It's like rock paper scissors; recognize what your enemy's strengths and weaknesses are, as well as your own."|313|0
units.english: "It's like rock paper scissors; recognize what your enemy's strengths and weaknesses are, as well as your own."
units.italian: "È come carta forbice sasso: riconosci i punti di forza e di debolezza del tuo nemico, oltre ai tuoi."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade end|As you land on <planet>, James says, "Well, you made it in one piece! Still think you want to be piloting an interceptor?"|319|0
units.english: As you land on <planet>, James says, "Well, you made it in one piece! Still think you want to be piloting an interceptor?"
units.italian: Mentre atterri su <planet>, James dice: "Beh, sei arrivato tutto intero! Pensi ancora di voler pilotare un intercettore?"

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade end|	"Sure, but I can't wait until I've got a ship big enough to stand up to pirates instead of running from them."|321|0
units.english: "Sure, but I can't wait until I've got a ship big enough to stand up to pirates instead of running from them."
units.italian: "Certo, ma non vedo l'ora di avere una nave abbastanza grande da affrontare i pirati invece di scappare."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade end|	"Well, maybe I should've bought a freighter instead."|322|0
units.english: "Well, maybe I should've bought a freighter instead."
units.italian: "Beh, forse avrei dovuto comprare un mercantile."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade end|	"Better start saving up then," he says. "I know a number of old Sparrow pilots who made their first million credits mining asteroids before they could afford a more combat-worthy ship. They had to look around for a while before finding a system with any asteroids worth mining, but it was worth it. Anyway, let's go get your payment." You walk out of the ship and sign the papers to hand off the <commodity> to the dock workers on <planet>. They hand you a credit chip worth <payment>.|323|0
units.english: "Better start saving up then," he says. "I know a number of old Sparrow pilots who made their first million credits mining asteroids before they could afford a more combat-worthy ship. They had to look around for a while before finding a system with any asteroids worth mining, but it was worth it. Anyway, let's go get your payment." You walk out of the ship and sign the papers to hand off the <commodity> to the dock workers on <planet>. They hand you a credit chip worth <payment>.
units.italian: "Meglio che inizi a mettere da parte," dice. "Conosco diversi vecchi piloti di Sparrow che hanno fatto il loro primo milione di crediti estraendo asteroidi prima di potersi permettere una nave più adatta al combattimento. Hanno dovuto cercare un po' prima di trovare un sistema con asteroidi che valessero l'estrazione, ma ne è valsa la pena. Comunque, andiamo a prendere il tuo pagamento." Esci dalla nave e firmi le carte per consegnare <commodity> agli scaricatori di <planet>. Ti consegnano un chip di credito da <payment>.

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade end|	"I've got an idea for something you might want to try," says James. "Meet me in the spaceport bar in a little while."|324|0
units.english: "I've got an idea for something you might want to try," says James. "Meet me in the spaceport bar in a little while."
units.italian: "Ho un'idea su qualcosa che potresti voler provare," dice James. "Raggiungimi al bar dello spazioporto fra un po'."

units.id: conversation:interceptor evade end|	"I've got an idea for something you might want to try," says James. "Meet me in the spaceport bar in a little while. And make sure you have a weapon installed; you should be able to buy one in <planet>'s outfitter."|327|0
units.english: "I've got an idea for something you might want to try," says James. "Meet me in the spaceport bar in a little while. And make sure you have a weapon installed; you should be able to buy one in <planet>'s outfitter."
units.italian: "Ho un'idea su qualcosa che potresti voler provare," dice James. "Raggiungimi al bar dello spazioporto fra un po'. E assicurati di avere un'arma installata; dovresti poterla comprare dal fornitore di <planet>."

units.id: conversation:mining intro|You find James waiting for you just outside the spaceport bar. Against the steady patter of micrometeorites against the roof he tells you, "Working here on <origin> is one of the few jobs in the galaxy more dangerous than fighting pirates. And worse, because if a big meteorite decides to strike this station, there's basically nothing the miners can do about it except hope they see it coming." He turns to you with a grin. "But nonetheless, I think you might be interested in this idea."|336|0
units.english: You find James waiting for you just outside the spaceport bar. Against the steady patter of micrometeorites against the roof he tells you, "Working here on <origin> is one of the few jobs in the galaxy more dangerous than fighting pirates. And worse, because if a big meteorite decides to strike this station, there's basically nothing the miners can do about it except hope they see it coming." He turns to you with a grin. "But nonetheless, I think you might be interested in this idea."
units.italian: Trovi James che ti aspetta appena fuori dal bar dello spazioporto. Sul ticchettio costante dei micrometeoriti contro il tetto ti dice: "Lavorare qui su <origin> è uno dei pochi mestieri della galassia più pericolosi che combattere i pirati. E peggio, perché se un meteorite grosso decidesse di colpire questa stazione, i minatori non possono fare praticamente nulla se non sperare di vederlo arrivare." Si volta verso di te con un ghigno. "Ciò nonostante, credo che questa idea potrebbe interessarti."

units.id: conversation:mining intro|Similar to Delve, <origin>'s spaceport is embedded in solid rock, but that is where the similarities end. Where Delve's spaceport was utilitarian, Ada finds space to flex its wealth by turning the industrial elements of rock and metal into elegant architecture. The nightmarish take-off and landing angles one might expect from a spaceport set in a canyon wall are missing, replaced by spacious and well-marked flight paths. The smell of oil and steel pervasive in many Syndicate ports is suppressed by crisp air supplied by the local environmental control systems.|339|0
units.english: Similar to Delve, <origin>'s spaceport is embedded in solid rock, but that is where the similarities end. Where Delve's spaceport was utilitarian, Ada finds space to flex its wealth by turning the industrial elements of rock and metal into elegant architecture. The nightmarish take-off and landing angles one might expect from a spaceport set in a canyon wall are missing, replaced by spacious and well-marked flight paths. The smell of oil and steel pervasive in many Syndicate ports is suppressed by crisp air supplied by the local environmental control systems.
units.italian: Come a Delve, lo spazioporto di <origin> è incassato nella roccia viva, ma le somiglianze finiscono lì. Dove quello di Delve era utilitario, Ada trova lo spazio per ostentare la propria ricchezza trasformando gli elementi industriali di pietra e metallo in architettura elegante. Gli angoli di decollo e atterraggio da incubo che ci si aspetterebbe da uno spazioporto scavato nella parete di un canyon qui mancano, sostituiti da corridoi di volo ampi e ben segnalati. L'odore di olio e acciaio tipico di molti porti del Sindacato è soppresso dall'aria fresca fornita dagli impianti locali di controllo ambientale.

units.id: conversation:mining intro|	James leads you down the side of the bar to a booth where a man with a half-eaten hamburger and a plate of fries is sitting, busily examining a star map of the local sector. He notices your arrival and stands up to greet you. "<first>, this is Captain Marshall," James says as you shake his hand. "I told him about your new ship and how it'd be a good idea for you to get a taste of asteroid mining. He mines in this part of space and says there's a good system nearby if you're willing to give it a try."|342|0
units.english: James leads you down the side of the bar to a booth where a man with a half-eaten hamburger and a plate of fries is sitting, busily examining a star map of the local sector. He notices your arrival and stands up to greet you. "<first>, this is Captain Marshall," James says as you shake his hand. "I told him about your new ship and how it'd be a good idea for you to get a taste of asteroid mining. He mines in this part of space and says there's a good system nearby if you're willing to give it a try."
units.italian: James ti guida lungo il lato del bar fino a un separé dove è seduto un uomo con un hamburger a metà e un piatto di patatine, intento a esaminare una carta stellare del settore locale. Nota il tuo arrivo e si alza a salutarti. "<first>, lui è il capitano Marshall," dice James mentre gli stringi la mano. "Gli ho parlato della tua nuova nave e di come sarebbe una buona idea che ti facessi un po' di esperienza nell'estrazione degli asteroidi. Lui estrae in questa parte di spazio e dice che c'è un buon sistema qui vicino, se te la senti di provare."

units.id: conversation:mining intro|The world of <origin> is in full bloom; the fields that the spaceport overlooks are filled with flowers of every color of the rainbow, and a sweet smell rests in the air. You end up finding James in one of the spaceport's gardens, and he waves you over to a table with a woman who is finishing off a steak. On the far side of the table is a map covered in annotations. As you get closer, the woman notices your arrival, wipes her mouth, and offers her hand.|346|0

units.italian: Il mondo di <origin> è in pieno fiore: i campi che lo spazioporto domina sono pieni di fiori di tutti i colori dell'arcobaleno, e nell'aria resta un profumo dolce. Finisci per trovare James in uno dei giardini dello spazioporto, e ti fa cenno di avvicinarti a un tavolo con una donna che sta finendo una bistecca. Sul lato opposto del tavolo c'è una mappa piena di annotazioni. Avvicinandoti, la donna nota il tuo arrivo, si asciuga la bocca e ti porge la mano.

units.id: conversation:mining intro|	"Mining sounds interesting. I'll give it a shot."|351|0
units.english: "Mining sounds interesting. I'll give it a shot."

units.id: conversation:mining intro|	"I think I'm ready to head out on my own."|352|0
units.english: "I think I'm ready to head out on my own."
units.italian: "Credo di essere pronto a partire da solo."

units.id: conversation:mining intro|	"That's good to hear," Captain <captain> says with a smile. "But be warned that mining isn't as easy as one might think. Especially without an asteroid scanner, mining can be just as much a test of your piloting skills as combat.|354|0
units.english: "That's good to hear," Captain <captain> says with a smile. "But be warned that mining isn't as easy as one might think. Especially without an asteroid scanner, mining can be just as much a test of your piloting skills as combat.
units.italian: "È bello sentirlo," dice il capitano <captain> con un sorriso. "Ma sappi che estrarre non è facile come si potrebbe pensare. Soprattutto senza uno scanner per asteroidi, l'estrazione può mettere alla prova le tue capacità di pilota quanto il combattimento.

units.id: conversation:mining intro|	"The first challenge," <they> continues, "will be finding which asteroids are valuable. The worthless asteroids are either brown and smooth or gray and spiky with no apparent orbit. It doesn't matter how long you shoot them, they won't be destroyed. Valuable asteroids will always orbit the star and have a range of colors and surface textures. If you're not sure which are which and you don't have an asteroid scanner to tell you, keep a look out for other miners to see what they're firing at.|355|0
units.english: "The first challenge," <they> continues, "will be finding which asteroids are valuable. The worthless asteroids are either brown and smooth or gray and spiky with no apparent orbit. It doesn't matter how long you shoot them, they won't be destroyed. Valuable asteroids will always orbit the star and have a range of colors and surface textures. If you're not sure which are which and you don't have an asteroid scanner to tell you, keep a look out for other miners to see what they're firing at.
units.italian: "La prima difficoltà," continua, "sarà capire quali asteroidi sono preziosi. Gli asteroidi inutili sono marroni e lisci, oppure grigi e appuntiti, senza un'orbita apparente. Non importa quanto a lungo spari: non si distruggono. Gli asteroidi preziosi orbitano sempre intorno alla stella e hanno una varietà di colori e texture superficiali. Se non sei sicuro di quali siano e non hai uno scanner per asteroidi che te lo dica, tieni d'occhio gli altri minatori per vedere che cosa colpiscono.

units.id: conversation:mining intro|	"Generally speaking, the more valuable minerals are tougher to mine, either because they're harder to break apart, or they're less common and in more dangerous regions of the galaxy. Silicon breaks up quickly; you'll fill your hold in a hurry and the stuff is everywhere. Platinum or gold asteroids are more work; they're not as common in areas where the Navy watches your back, but you make several times the number of credits for the effort.|356|0

units.italian: "In generale, i minerali più preziosi sono più difficili da estrarre, perché si rompono con più fatica, oppure sono meno comuni e si trovano in regioni più pericolose della galassia. Il silicio si sbriciola in fretta: riempirai la stiva in un attimo e ce n'è ovunque. Gli asteroidi di platino o oro richiedono più lavoro; non sono così comuni nelle zone dove la Marina ti guarda le spalle, ma ti fruttano diversi volte i crediti per lo sforzo.

units.id: conversation:mining intro|	"I could go on, but I think you get the picture."|357|0
units.english: "I could go on, but I think you get the picture."
units.italian: "Potrei continuare, ma credo che tu abbia capito."

units.id: conversation:mining intro|	You and James chat with <captain> a while longer, and <they> suggests trying your hand at mining in <system>. "It's a great place. You could throw a dart in that system and half the time you'd hit an asteroid worth at least something, and I've never been bothered by pirates while I've been there. The easiest asteroids to get there are the silicon ones; you can spot them by their slightly-green tint."|363|0

units.italian: Tu e James chiacchierate ancora un po' con <captain>, e alla fine ti suggerisce di provare a estrarre in <system>. "È un gran posto. Lanci un dardo in quel sistema e metà delle volte colpiresti un asteroide che vale almeno qualcosa, e non sono mai stato importunato dai pirati mentre ero là. Gli asteroidi più facili da trovare sono quelli di silicio; li riconosci da una leggera tinta verdastra."

units.id: conversation:mining intro|	"That does sound like a good place for a beginner pilot," James says. "How about we start small, <first>? Let's go mine at least five tons of silicon before landing on <planet> and we can call it a day."|364|0
units.english: "That does sound like a good place for a beginner pilot," James says. "How about we start small, <first>? Let's go mine at least five tons of silicon before landing on <planet> and we can call it a day."
